drivingQuestion: Does a dislocated femur or wing render a bird a tereifa, and by what sign is an animal shown to be a tereifa?
outcomeNote: Twice settled by decision formulae: the halakha follows none of the amoraic statements on a dislocated femur but R' Yehoshua ben Levi's line (57b.6), and the sign of a doubtful tereifa is fixed as twelve months for a male and giving birth for a female (58a.14); the eggs question ends with two rival versions of Ameimar left standing side by side.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָד בַּבְּהֵמָה – כְּשֵׁרָה, שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בַּבְּהֵמָה – טְרֵפָה, שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף – טְרֵפָה, שְׁמוּטַת גַּף בָּעוֹף – טְרֵפָה, חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא נִיקְּבָה הָרֵיאָה. וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: תִּיבָּדֵק, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תִּיבָּדֵק.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says: A dislocated foreleg in an animal is kosher. A dislocated femur in an animal» renders it «a tereifa. A dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa. A dislocated wing in a bird» renders it «a tereifa,» because «we» must be «concerned» that «perhaps the lung was perforated.» The lung is located near the wing’s attachment to the body, and part of the lung may have been torn out with the wing. «And Shmuel says:» The lung «should be inspected,» and if no damage is found, the bird is kosher. «And so says Rabbi Yoḥanan: It should be inspected.»

segments.he: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: אֵין רֵיאָה לָעוֹף, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יֵשׁ לוֹ וְיֶשְׁנָהּ כְּעָלֶה שֶׁל וֶורֶד בֵּין אֲגַפַּיִם. מַאי ״אֵין רֵיאָה לָעוֹף״? אִילֵּימָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ כְּלָל – וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּאִית לֵיהּ! אֶלָּא דְּלָא מִיטְּרִיף בֵּיהּ, וְהָתָנֵי לֵוִי: טְרֵפוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים בַּבְּהֵמָה – כְּנֶגְדָּן בָּעוֹף, יָתֵר עֲלֵיהֶן עוֹף נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ!
segments.en: «Ḥizkiyya,» son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, «says: A bird has no lungs. And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» A bird «does have» lungs, «and they are like a rose petal» in appearance, thin and red, «between the wings.» The Gemara asks: «What» does Ḥizkiyya mean when he says that «a bird has no lungs? If we say that it has no» lungs «at all,» that is problematic, as «don’t we see that it does have» lungs? «Rather,» say that he means «that» the bird «is not rendered a tereifa by them» if they are perforated. But this, too, is problematic, as «doesn’t Levi teach:» Those «tereifot that the Sages enumerated in an animal» hold «likewise in a bird,» and «in addition to those, a bird» is a tereifa if «the bone» of the skull «was broken, even if the membrane of the brain was not perforated?» If so, a perforated lung in a bird, as in an animal, renders it a tereifa.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, אֵין לוֹ לֹא לִינָּפֵל וְלֹא לֵיחָמֵר. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר רַב חָנָה: הוֹאִיל וְרוֹב צַלְעוֹתֶיהָ מְגִינּוֹת עָלֶיהָ.
segments.en: «Rather,» say that Ḥizkiyya means that a bird’s lung «has no» halakha of «falling and no» halakha of «singeing.» If a bird falls, one need not inspect the lungs for damage as he must other organs (see 51b), and if it falls in a fire, one need not inspect the lungs for a change in color as he must other organs (see 56b). «What is the reason» for this? «Rav Ḥana said: Since a majority of» the bird’s «ribs protect» the lungs, one need not be concerned that the lung was damaged.

segments.he: וְהָא מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יֵשׁ לוֹ, וְיֶשְׁנָהּ כְּעָלֶה שֶׁל וֶורֶד בֵּין אֲגַפַּיִים – מִכְּלָל דְּחִזְקִיָּה סָבַר דְּלֵית לֵיהּ! אֶלָּא אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִדְּבָרָיו שֶׁל בְּרִיבִּי נִיכָּר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי בְּתַרְנְגוֹלִין.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But from» the fact «that Rabbi Yoḥanan says» in response: A bird «does have» lungs, «and they are like a rose petal between the wings, by inference» one must conclude «that Ḥizkiyya maintains that it has no» lungs at all. «Rather,» one must say as «they say in the West,» Eretz Yisrael, «in the name of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina: From the statement of the Distinguished,» i.e., Ḥizkiyya, «it is apparent that he is unfamiliar with chickens.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף כְּשֵׁרָה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא: וְהָא רַבָּנַן דַּאֲתוֹ מִפּוּמְבְּדִיתָא אֲמַרוּ רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף טְרֵפָה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּרִי, נַהֲרָא נַהֲרָא וּפְשָׁטֵיהּ.
segments.en: § «Rav Huna said» that «Rav said: A dislocated femur in a bird is kosher. Rabba bar Rav Huna said to Rav Huna: But the Rabbis that came from Pumbedita said» that «Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav: A dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa.» Rav Huna «said to him: My son, each river and its course,» i.e., different communities observe different customs. Although Rav himself held that such a bird is kosher, he ruled for those living in Pumbedita that such a bird is a tereifa, in accordance with their own custom.

segments.he: אֲזַל רַבִּי אַבָּא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא דְּקָא בָּדֵיק בְּצוֹמֶת הַגִּידִין. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמָר כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָא רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף כְּשֵׁרָה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא מַתְנִיתִין יָדַעְנָא: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּחְתְּכוּ רַגְלֶיהָ מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַטָּה כְּשֵׁרָה, מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה פְּסוּלָה, וְכֵן שֶׁנִּיטַּל צוֹמֶת הַגִּידִין, וְאָמַר רַב עֲלַהּ: וְכֵן בָּעוֹף.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts: «Rabbi Abba went» and «found Rav Yirmeya bar Abba inspecting» birds «at the convergence of sinews» in the thigh. Rabbi Abba «said to him: Why» must «Master» do «all this? But doesn’t Rav Huna say» that «Rav» says: «A dislocated femur in a bird is kosher?» If a bird is kosher even when the whole thigh has been removed, all the more so it should be kosher when only the convergence of sinews has been removed. Rav Yirmeya bar Abba «said to him: I know the mishna» (76a): With regard to «an animal whose hind legs were severed,» if they were severed «from the leg joint and below,» it is «kosher; from the leg joint and above,» it is a tereifa and «unfit» for consumption. «And likewise» an animal whose «convergence of sinews» in the thigh «was removed» is a tereifa. «And Rav said about this: And likewise with regard to a bird.»

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב! אִישְׁתִּיק. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְמָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ בֵּין שְׁמוּטָה לַחֲתוּכָה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאַתְּ מְפָרְשַׁתְּ שְׁמַעְתָּתֵיהּ דְּרַב? בְּפֵירוּשׁ אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטָה – כְּשֵׁרָה, חֲתוּכָה – פְּסוּלָה. וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי חוֹתְכָהּ מִכָּאן וָמֵתָה, חוֹתְכָהּ מִכָּאן וְחָיְתָה.
segments.en: Rabbi Abba responded: «If so,» this statement «of Rav,» that a bird whose convergence of sinews was removed is a tereifa, poses «a difficulty for» that statement «of Rav,» that a bird with a dislocated femur is kosher. Rav Yirmeya bar Abba «was silent» and did not respond. Rabbi Abba «said to him: Perhaps there is a difference for» Rav «between a dislocated» femur «and a severed» femur, and while the former does not render a bird a tereifa, the latter does. Rav Yirmeya bar Abba «said to him: And are you interpreting Rav’s halakhot» based on your own reasoning? «Rav said explicitly: A dislocated» femur «is kosher,» while «a severed» femur renders the animal «unfit» for consumption. «And do not be confounded» by this distinction, «as» one «cuts» an animal «from here,» in one place, «and it dies,» but one «cuts it from there,» in another place, «and it lives.»

segments.he: כִּי סְלֵיק רַבִּי אַבָּא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף טְרֵפָה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיֵּי דְּמָר, מִיּוֹמָא דִּסְלֵיק מָר לְהָכָא
segments.en: The Gemara recounts: «When Rabbi Abba went up» from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, «he found Rabbi Zeira sitting and saying: Rav Huna said» that «Rav said» that «a dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa.» Rabbi Abba «said to him:» By «Master’s life, since the day that Master came up to here,» Eretz Yisrael,

segments.he: הֲוָה לַן פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא וּשְׁאֵילְנֵיהּ, וַאֲמַר לַן: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף כְּשֵׁירָה.
segments.en: «we had the opportunity to speak with Rav Huna, and we asked him» about this matter, «and he said to us: A dislocated femur in a bird is kosher.»

segments.he: וְאַשְׁכַּחְתֵּיהּ נָמֵי לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא דְּיָתֵיב וְקָא בָדֵיק בְּצוֹמֵת הַגִּידִין, וְאַקְשִׁי לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף כְּשֵׁרָה? אָמַר לִי: אֲנָא מַתְנִיתִין יָדַעְנָא: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּחְתְּכוּ רַגְלֶיהָ, מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמִטָּה – כְּשֵׁרָה, מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה – פְּסוּלָה, וְכֵן שֶׁנִּיטַּל צוֹמֶת הַגִּידִין, וְאָמַר רַב עֲלַהּ: וְכֵן בָּעוֹף.
segments.en: «And I also found Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba sitting and inspecting» birds «at the convergence of sinews» in the thigh. «And I» posed «a difficulty to him: Doesn’t Master maintain» in accordance with «this» statement «that Rav Huna says» that «Rav says: A dislocated femur in a bird is kosher?» Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba «said to me: I know the mishna» (76a): With regard to «an animal whose hind legs were severed,» if they were severed «from the leg joint and below,» it is «kosher; from the leg joint and above,» it is a tereifa and «unfit» for consumption. «And likewise» an animal whose «convergence of sinews» in the thigh «was removed» is a tereifa. «And Rav said about this: And likewise with regard to a bird.»

segments.he: וַאֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב! אִישְׁתִּיק, וְאַקְשַׁי לֵיהּ: וְדִלְמָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַב בֵּין שְׁמוּטָה לַחֲתוּכָה? וְאָמַר לִי: וְאַתְּ מְפָרְשַׁתְּ שְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב? בְּפֵירוּשׁ אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטָה – כְּשֵׁרָה, חֲתוּכָה – פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: «And I said to him: If so,» this statement «of Rav» poses «a difficulty for» that statement «of Rav.» Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba «was silent. And I challenged him: But perhaps there is a difference for Rav between a dislocated» femur «and a severed» one. «And he said to me: And are you interpreting Rav’s halakha» based on your own reasoning? «Rav said explicitly: A dislocated» femur «is kosher,» while «a severed» femur renders the animal «unfit» for consumption.

segments.he: וְאַתְּ, מָה בִּידָךְ? הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף טְרֵפָה, וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: Rabbi Abba then asked Rabbi Zeira: «And» as for «you, what is in your hand?» What have you heard with regard to this halakha? Rabbi Zeira «said to him: This» is what «Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi says» that «Rav says: A dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa. And so said Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי: אִילְמָלֵי הֲוָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּאַתְרָא דְּאוֹרוֹ בַּהּ חַבְרָוָותָא לְהֶתֵּירָא, לָא פַּרְכֵּיס. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף כְּשֵׁרָה. וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא שֶׁנִּשְׁמְטָה יָרֵךְ שֶׁלָּהּ, וֶהֱבִיאָהּ לִפְנֵי רַבִּי וְהִתִּירָהּ לוֹ, וּמְלָחָהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וַהֲוָה מוֹרֵי בַּהּ הֲלָכָה לַתַּלְמִידִים: זֶה הִתִּיר לִי רַבִּי, זֶה הִתִּיר לִי רַבִּי.
segments.en: «And» with regard to this, «Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said: If Rabbi Yoḥanan had been in the place where the assembly ruled to permit» such a bird, he would «not» have «stirred.» In other words, he would not have contested their ruling, because they were the greatest Sages of the previous generation. «As Rabbi Ḥanina says» that «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «says: A dislocated femur in a bird is kosher. And Rabbi Ḥanina had a hen whose femur was dislocated, and he brought it before Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi, «and» Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi «permitted it to him, and Rabbi Ḥanina salted» the hen to preserve it. «And he would teach the students the halakha with it,» as he would show them the preserved body of the hen and say: «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «permitted this to me, Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «permitted this to me.»

segments.he: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא, אֶלָּא כִּי הָא דִּשְׁאֵל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: קְדִירַת קָנֶה בְּכַמָּה? אָמַר לוֹ: מִשְׁנָה שְׁלֵמָה שָׁנִינוּ, עַד כְּאִיסָּר הָאִיטַלְקִי. אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא רָחֵל אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּשְׁכוּנָתֵנוּ שֶׁנִּקְדַּר קָנֶה שֶׁלָּהּ, וְעָשׂוּ לָהּ קְרוּמִין שֶׁל קָנֶה וְחָיְתָה!
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: «But the halakha» is «not in accordance with any of these statements. Rather,» it is «in accordance with that which Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: In what amount» must «a windpipe» be «punctured» to render the animal a tereifa? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi «said to him: We learned a full mishna» (54a): «Until» the perforation is the same size «as the Italian issar.» Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai «said to him: But wasn’t there a certain ewe in our neighborhood whose windpipe was punctured» in a greater amount, «and they made» a seal «for» the windpipe out of «the shell of a reed and it lived?»

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ: וְעַל דָּא אַתְּ סָמֵיךְ? וַהֲלֹא הֲלָכָה רוֹוַחַת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: שְׁמוּטַת יָרֵךְ בָּעוֹף טְרֵפָה, וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא שֶׁנִּשְׁמְטָה יָרֵךְ שֶׁלָּהּ, וְעָשׂוּ לָהּ שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל קָנֶה וְחָיְתָה! אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר: תּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה, הָכָא נָמֵי תּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה.
segments.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi «said to him: And do you rely on this» incident as evidence? «But isn’t it a widespread halakha among the Jewish people» that «a dislocated femur in a bird» renders it «a tereifa? And» still, «Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta had a hen whose femur was dislocated, and they made it» a support out of the «tube of a reed and it lived. Rather, what have you to say» about this case? It must have «occurred within twelve months» of the dislocation, and afterward the hen died, since no tereifa can live more than twelve months. «Here, too,» in the case of the punctured windpipe, the episode «occurred within twelve months» of the injury and the ewe later died.

segments.he: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא שֶׁעַסְקָן בִּדְבָרִים הָיָה, וְהָיָה עוֹשֶׂה דָּבָר לְהוֹצִיא מִלִּבּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם נִיטְּלָה הַנּוֹצָה פְּסוּלָה. וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה נוֹצָה שֶׁלָּהּ, וְהִנִּיחָה בַּתַּנּוּר, וְטָלָה עָלֶיהָ בְּמַטְלִית שֶׁל טַרְסִיִּים, וְגִידְּלָה כְּנָפַיִים הָאַחֲרוֹנִים יוֹתֵר מִן הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
segments.en: § «They said about Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta that he was a researcher of» various «matters, and he would act to counter the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, as Rabbi Yehuda would say: If the down» covering a bird’s body «was removed,» it is a tereifa and «unfit» for consumption, as stated in the mishna. «And Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta had a hen whose down was removed, and he placed it in an oven,» a warm place, «and he covered it with a Coppersmiths’ [tarsiyyim] apron, and its new,» i.e., rehabilitated, «wings grew» even «more» feathers «than the original» wings.

segments.he: וְדִלְמָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה טְרֵפָה מַשְׁבַּחַת? אִם כֵּן, בְּמִידֵּי דְּמִיטַּרְפָא בַּהּ – הִגְדִּילָה כְּנָפַיִים הָאַחֲרוֹנִים יוֹתֵר מִן הָרִאשׁוֹנִים?!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But» how does this counter Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion? «Perhaps Rabbi Yehuda holds» that «a tereifa» can live and that its health can even «improve» beyond its previous state. The Gemara responds: Even «if» this is «so,» would Rabbi Yehuda say so «with regard to the» very «thing» with «which it was rendered a tereifa,» as is the case here, where «it grew new wings» with «more» feathers «than the original» wings?

segments.he: מַאי עַסְקָן בִּדְבָרִים? אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֵךְ אֶל נְמָלָה עָצֵל רְאֵה דְרָכֶיהָ וַחֲכָם, אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהּ קָצִין שֹׁטֵר וּמֹשֵׁל, תָּכִין בַּקַּיִץ לַחְמָהּ״. אָמַר: אֵיזִיל אִיחְזֵי אִי וַדַּאי הוּא דְּלֵית לְהוּ מַלְכָּא!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: From «what» episode did Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta earn the title: «Researcher of matters? Rav Mesharshiyya said:» He saw «that it is written: “Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer”» (Proverbs 6:6–8). Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta «said: I will go and see if it is correct that they have no king.»

segments.he: אֲזַל בִּתְקוּפַת תַּמּוּז, פַּרְסֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ אַקִּינָּא דְּשׁוּמְשְׁמָנֵי. נְפַק אֲתָא חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ, אַתְנַח בֵּיהּ סִימָנָא. עָל, אֲמַר לְהוּ: ״נְפַל טוּלָּא״. נְפַקוּ וַאֲתוֹ, דַּלְיֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ, נְפַל שִׁמְשָׁא. נְפַלוּ עֲלֵיהּ וְקַטְלֵיהּ. אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לֵית לְהוּ מַלְכָּא, דְּאִי אִית לְהוּ הַרְמָנָא דְּמַלְכָּא לָא לִיבְעוֹ.
segments.en: «He went in the season of Tammuz,» i.e., summer. Knowing that ants avoid intense heat, «he spread his cloak over an ant hole» to provide shade. «One of» the ants «came out» and saw the shade. Rabbi Shimon «placed a distinguishing mark on» the ant. «It went into» the hole and «said to» the other ants: «Shade has fallen. They» all «came out» to work. Rabbi Shimon «lifted up his cloak,» and «the sun fell» on them. They all «fell upon» the first ant «and killed it. He said:» One may «learn from» their actions that «they have no king; as, if they had a king, would they not need the king’s edict [harmana]» to execute their fellow ant?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְדִלְמָא מַלְכָּא הֲוָה בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ? אִי נָמֵי, הַרְמָנָא דְּמַלְכָּא הֲווֹ נְקִיטִי? אִי נָמֵי בֵּין מַלְכָּא לְמַלְכָּא הֲוָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם אֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה״? אֶלָּא, סְמוֹךְ אַהֵימָנוּתָא דִּשְׁלֹמֹה.
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: But perhaps the king was with them» at the time and gave them permission. «Or» perhaps «they» already «possessed the king’s edict» giving them license to kill the ant. «Or» perhaps it «was» an interregnum «between kings, as it is written: “In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes”» (Judges 17:6). «Rather, rely on the credibility of Solomon,» the author of Proverbs, that ants have no king.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: סִימָן לִטְרֵפָה – שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ. מֵיתִיבִי: סִימָן לִטְרֵפָה – כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מַשְׁבַּחַת וְהוֹלֶכֶת – בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהִיא כְּשֵׁרָה, מִתְנַוְּונָה וְהוֹלֶכֶת – בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהִיא טְרֵפָה. רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: סִימָן לִטְרֵפָה – שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא הַרְבֵּה מִתְקַיְּימוֹת שְׁתַּיִם שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים!
segments.en: § «Rav Huna says: The sign of a tereifa» is «twelve months.» If it is uncertain whether an animal is a tereifa, one may wait twelve months; if the animal survives, it is kosher. The Gemara «raises an objection» from a baraita: «The sign of a tereifa» is «any» animal «that cannot give birth. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:» If its health «improves continuously, it is certainly kosher;» if its health «deteriorates continuously, it is certainly a tereifa. Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «says: The sign of a tereifa» is any animal that does not survive «thirty days.» The Sages «said to him: But don’t many» animals that are certainly tereifot «survive two» or «three years?» None of the opinions cited in the baraita accord with Rav Huna’s statement.

segments.he: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: וּבַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת, עַד שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ נֶקֶב אֶחָד אָרוֹךְ, אֲפִילּוּ נְקָבִים הַרְבֵּה מִצְטָרְפִים לִמְלֹא מַקְדֵּחַ. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּעִנְבּוּל, בְּאֶחָד שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה גֻּלְגׇּלְתּוֹ, וְעָשׂוּ לוֹ חִידּוּק שֶׁל קֵרוּיָה וְחָיָה. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה? יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה הָיָה, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלָיו יְמוֹת הַצִּנָּה מִיָּד מֵת.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: The matter «is» a dispute between «tanna’im, as it is taught» in a baraita: «And in a skull that contains one long hole,» or «even» if it has «many holes,» the areas of the holes «join together to» constitute the «size of a drill hole,» and they render the animal a tereifa. «Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam said:» There was «an incident in» a place called «Inbul involving one whose skull was missing» a piece, «and they made for him» a patch out of «the shell of a gourd, and he survived.» Therefore, an animal with a missing piece of skull cannot be a tereifa. «Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said to him:» Can you bring «proof from there? It was summer» then, «and once winter came upon him he died immediately.» Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds that an animal is a tereifa if it does not survive through summer and winter, i.e., one year. Rav Huna’s statement accords with this opinion.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, הֲלָכָה: טְרֵפָה יוֹלֶדֶת וּמַשְׁבַּחַת. אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הָנֵי בֵּיעֵי דִּטְרֵפָה
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov says:» The «halakha» is that «a tereifa can give birth and» its health can even «improve.» If the animal appears to recover or gives birth, this does not prove it is not a tereifa. «Ameimar says:» With regard to «these eggs of a tereifa» bird,

segments.he: שִׁיחְלָא קַמָּא אֲסִירָא, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ – הָוֵה לֵיהּ זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם, וּמוּתָּר.
segments.en: «the first clutch [shiḥala]» of eggs that were in its body at the time it was rendered a tereifa «is prohibited» for consumption, because these eggs are considered part of the bird and were therefore rendered tereifa along with it. But as for any egg fertilized «from this» point «forward, it is» a case where both «this and that cause» it, i.e., a tereifa female and a kosher male, «and» as a rule, when permitted and prohibited causes operate together, the joint result is «permitted.»

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: וְשָׁוִין בְּבֵיצַת טְרֵיפָה שֶׁאֲסוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁגָּדְלָה בְּאִיסּוּר! הָתָם בִּדְסָפְנָא מֵאַרְעָא.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi raised an objection to Ameimar» from a mishna (Eduyyot 5:1): «And» all «agree with regard to the egg of a tereifa» bird «that it is prohibited» for consumption, «because it grew in» a state of «prohibition.» Evidently, even eggs created after the bird was rendered a tereifa are prohibited. Ameimar said to him: «There,» the mishna is dealing «with» a bird «that is heated by the earth,» i.e., that was not fertilized by a male, and the female tereifa is therefore the sole source of the egg.

segments.he: וְלִישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ בְּשִׁיחְלָא קַמָּא? אִם כֵּן, ״גָּדְלָה״? ״גָּמְרָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «And let» Ameimar «answer» differently, that the mishna is dealing «with the first clutch» of eggs, which were part of the mother’s body when it became a tereifa. The Gemara responds: «If» this was «so,» why does the mishna state: Because «it grew» in a state of prohibition? The mishna «should have» stated: Because it «was finished» in a state of prohibition.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, הָא דִּתְנַן: וְלַד טְרֵפָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִקְרַב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יִקְרַב. בְּמַאי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי? בְּשֶׁנִּטְרְפָה וּלְבַסּוֹף עִיבְּרָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר. אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי לְגָבוֹהַּ, לִיפַּלְגוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט?
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But» if the offspring in the womb of an animal becomes a tereifa along with it, then «that which we learned» in a baraita is difficult: With regard to the «offspring of a tereifa, Rabbi Eliezer says» that «it shall not be sacrificed on the altar, and Rabbi Yehoshua says» that «it may be sacrificed. With regard to what» case do they «disagree?» It must be «with regard to» a case «where» the mother animal «was rendered a tereifa and afterward became pregnant» from a kosher male, and «Rabbi Eliezer holds:» In a case where «this and that cause» it, it is «prohibited, and Rabbi Yehoshua holds:» In a case where «this and that cause» it, it is «permitted.» But «if so, rather than disputing» whether it is permitted to sacrifice such offspring «to the Most High, let them disagree» concerning the more basic issue of whether the offspring is permitted «to an ordinary» person for consumption.

segments.he: לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְגָבוֹהַּ נָמֵי שָׁרֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: The dispute addresses the question of whether it is permitted to sacrifice the animal as an offering in order «to convey to you the far-reaching nature of» the lenient opinion «of Rabbi Yehoshua, that» such an animal is «permitted even» as an offering «to the Most High.»

segments.he: וְלִיפַּלְגוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט, לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט נָמֵי אָסַור! כֹּחַ דְּהֶיתֵּרָא עֲדִיף לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «But let them disagree» concerning whether the animal is permitted «to an ordinary» person in order «to convey to you the far-reaching nature» of the stringent opinion «of Rabbi Eliezer, that» such an animal «is prohibited even to an ordinary» person. The Gemara responds: It is «preferable for» the tanna to emphasize «the power of leniency.»

segments.he: וּמוֹדִים בְּבֵיצַת טְרֵפָה שֶׁאֲסוּרָה, בִּדְסָפְנָא מֵאַרְעָא, דְּחַד גּוֹרֵם הוּא.
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: Since Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree with regard to an offspring brought about by two causes, it follows that when the mishna states: «And» they «concede with regard to the egg of a tereifa» bird «that it is prohibited» for consumption, this is «referring to» a bird «that is heated by the earth» and was not fertilized by a male, so «that there is» only «one cause,» the tereifa mother bird.

segments.he: רַב אַחָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, וּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לִדְאַמֵּימָר כְּדַאֲמַרַן.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «Rav Aḥa holds in accordance with» the opinion of «Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov,» who said at the end of the previous amud that a tereifa animal can be capable of giving birth, and similarly a tereifa bird can be capable of laying eggs as well, «and he» therefore «teaches» the statement «of Ameimar as we have said,» that any egg fertilized after the bird became a tereifa is permitted.

segments.he: רָבִינָא לָא סָבַר לַהּ כִּדְרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, וּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לִדְאַמֵּימָר בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: הָנֵי בֵּיעֵי דִּסְפֵק טְרֵפָה, דְּשִׁיחְלָא קַמָּא מְשַׁהֵינַן לְהוּ, אִי הָדְרָה וְטָעֲנָה – שַׁרְיָין, וְאִי לָא – אֲסִירָן.
segments.en: But «Ravina does not hold in accordance with» the opinion of «Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov.» Rather, he holds that a tereifa cannot produce eggs or give birth. «And he» therefore «teaches» the statement «of Ameimar in this formulation: Ameimar said» that with regard to «these eggs of» a bird concerning which it is «uncertain» whether it is «a tereifa,» the halakha is as follows: «We leave» aside «the first clutch» of eggs. «If» the bird «produces» eggs «again,» the first eggs «are permitted» for consumption, because the bird is certainly not a tereifa. «And if not, they are prohibited,» because they were considered part of the bird when it was rendered a tereifa.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: וּמוֹדִים בְּבֵיצַת טְרֵפָה שֶׁאֲסוּרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁגָּדְלָה בְּאִיסּוּר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם בִּדְשִׁיחְלָא קַמָּא. אִם כֵּן, ״גָּדְלָה״? ״גָּמְרָה״ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! תְּנִי: גָּמְרָה.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi raised an objection to Ameimar» from a mishna (Eduyyot 5:1): «And they concede with regard to the egg of a tereifa» bird «that it is prohibited» for consumption, «because it grew in» a state of «prohibition.» Evidently, a tereifa bird can produce eggs. Ameimar «said to him:» The mishna «there» deals «with the first clutch» of eggs, which existed before the bird became a tereifa. Rav Ashi asks: «If so,» why does the mishna state: Because «it grew» in a state of prohibition? The mishna «should have» stated: Because it «was finished» in a state of prohibition. Ameimar responded: «Teach» an emended version of the mishna: Because it «was finished» in a state of prohibition.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, הָא דִּתְנַן: וְלַד טְרֵפָה, ר׳ אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִקְרַב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, ר׳ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יִקְרַב, בְּמַאי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי? כְּשֶׁעִיבְּרָה וּלְבַסּוֹף נִטְרְפָה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: עוּבָּר לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא. אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי לְגָבוֹהַּ, לִיפַּלְגוּ לְהֶדְיוֹט!
segments.en: Rav Ashi asks: «But» if a tereifa cannot become pregnant, «that which we learned» in a baraita is difficult: With regard to «the offspring of a tereifa, Rabbi Eliezer says» that «it shall not be sacrificed on the altar,» and «Rabbi Yehoshua says» that «it may be sacrificed. With regard to what» case do they «disagree?» It must be «with regard to» a case «where» the mother animal «became pregnant and» only «afterward was rendered a tereifa. Rabbi Eliezer holds» that «a fetus is» considered like «the thigh of its mother» and is rendered a tereifa as part of its body, «and Rabbi Yehoshua holds» that «a fetus is not» considered like «the thigh of its mother.» The Gemara objects: But «if so, rather than disputing» whether it is permitted to sacrifice such offspring «to the Most High, let them dispute» the more basic issue of whether the offspring is permitted «to an ordinary» person for consumption.

segments.he: לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ. וְלִיפַּלְגוּ בְּהֶדְיוֹט לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? כֹּחַ דְּהֶיתֵּירָא עֲדִיף לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: The mishna discusses the question of whether it is permitted to sacrifice the animal as an offering in order «to convey to you the far-reaching nature» of the lenient opinion «of Rabbi Yehoshua» that such an animal is permitted even as an offering to the Most High. The Gemara suggests: «But let them dispute» whether the animal is permitted «to an ordinary» person, in order «to convey to you the far-reaching nature» of the stringent opinion «of Rabbi Eliezer» that such an animal is prohibited even to an ordinary person. The Gemara responds: It is «preferable for» the tanna to emphasize «the power of leniency.»

segments.he: וּמוֹדִים וַדַּאי בְּבֵיצַת טְרֵיפָה שֶׁאֲסוּרָה, בִּדְשִׁיחְלָא קַמָּא, מַאי טַעְמָא? גּוּפַהּ הִיא.
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: According to this explanation, when the mishna states: «And they certainly concede with regard to the egg of a tereifa» bird «that it is prohibited» for consumption, it is dealing «with the first clutch» of eggs in the bird’s oviduct at the time it becomes a tereifa. Even Rabbi Yehoshua, who holds that the fetus of an animal is not considered like the thigh of its mother, concedes that a bird’s egg is rendered a tereifa along with it. «What is the reason» for this? Rabbi Yehoshua holds that an egg «is» a true part of «its body.»

segments.he: וְהִלְכְתָא בְּזָכָר – כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ, בִּנְקֵבָה – כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת.
segments.en: The Gemara rules: «And» with regard to an animal concerning which it is uncertain whether it is a tereifa, «the halakha» is: «In» the case of «a male,» it is prohibited for «an entire twelve-month» period. After that point, the animal is certainly kosher. «In» the case of «a female, any» animal «that does not give birth» is prohibited. Once it has, it is certainly kosher.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל (בְּרִיָּה) שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עֶצֶם אֵינוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַב הוּנָא, הָא דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: קִישּׁוּת (שהתליע) [שֶׁהִתְלִיעָה] בְּאִיבֶּיהָ אֲסוּרָה.
segments.en: § «Rav Huna says: Any creature that has no bones cannot last twelve months. Rav Pappa said:» One may «learn from Rav Huna’s» statement about «that which Shmuel says: If a serpent melon became infested by worms while attached to the ground» [«be’ibbeha»], the worm «is prohibited» for consumption, in accordance with the verse: “And every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth is a detestable thing; it shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 11:41).

segments.he: הָנֵי תַּמְרֵי דְּכַדָּא לְבָתַר תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא שַׁרְיָין.
segments.en: «These dates» stored in «a jar are permitted after» remaining there for «twelve months» of «the year.» Since worms have no bones, they cannot last twelve months. Consequently, any worms found in the dates must have hatched after they were picked and are therefore permitted.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב: לֵית בָּקָא בַּר יוֹמָא, וְלֵית דִּידְבָא בַּת שַׁתָּא.
segments.en: «Rav says: There is no one-day-old mosquito,» since all mosquitoes die before they have lived a day. «And there is no one-year-old fly.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְהָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: שַׁב שְׁנֵי אִימְּרַאי בָּקְתָּא מִבָּקָא. דְּאָמְרָה לֵיהּ: חֲזִיתֵיהּ לְבַר מָחוֹזָא דִּסְחָא בְּמַיָּא, וּסְלֵיק וְאִיכְּרֵךְ בִּסְדִינִין, וְאִיתֵּיבְתְּ עֲלֵיהּ וּמְצֵת מִינֵּיהּ, וְלָא הוֹדַעְתְּ לִי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, הָא דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי ״שִׁיתִּין מָנֵי פַּרְזְלָא תְּלוּ לֵיהּ לְבָקָא בְּקוּרְנָסֵיהּ״, מִי אִיכָּא? אִיהוּ גּוּפֵיהּ כַּמָּה הָוֵי? אֶלָּא בְּמָנֵי דִּידְהוּ, הָכָא נָמֵי בִּשְׁנֵי דִּידְהוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said to Abaye: But isn’t» there the adage that «people say» that «the female mosquito revolted against the male mosquito seven years, since she said to him: I saw a townsman swimming in the water, and he came out and wrapped himself in sheets, and you sat on him and sucked» blood «from him, and you did not inform me?» Apparently, some boneless creatures can survive at least seven years. Abaye «said to him: And according to your reasoning,» what about «that» adage «that people say: Six thousand iron dinars hang in a mosquito’s mallet,» i.e., its bite is powerful? «Is there» really such a thing? «How much does» the mosquito «itself» weigh? «Rather,» the saying must be referring «to hundreds of their own dinars,» i.e., the mosquitoes’ coins. «Here, too,» the adage is referring «to their own years,» not human years.

segments.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: בְּהֵמָה בַּעֲלַת חָמֵשׁ רַגְלַיִם, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לָהּ אֶלָּא שָׁלֹשׁ – הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד, אֲבָל חָסֵר וְיָתֵר בָּרֶגֶל – טְרֵפָה נָמֵי הָוְיָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? כׇּל יָתֵר כְּנָטוּל דָּמֵי.
segments.en: § «We learned» in a mishna «elsewhere» (Bekhorot 40a): «With regard to an animal with five legs, or» one «that has only three, this is a blemish,» and the animal may not be brought as an offering. «Rav Huna said: They taught» this halakha «only» in a case «where» the animal «was missing or had an additional foreleg. But» if it «was missing or had an additional hind leg, it is also a tereifa. What is the reason?» It is that «any extra» limb «is considered like a removed» limb. An animal whose foreleg was removed is kosher, but if its hind leg was removed it is a tereifa; the same applies if it had an extra leg.

segments.he: הָהִיא חֵיוְתָא דַּהֲוָה לַהּ תַּרְתֵּי סַנְיָא דֵּיבֵי, אַיְיתוּהָ לְרָבִינָא, וְטַרְפַהּ מִדְּרַב הוּנָא. וְאִי שָׁפְכָן לַהֲדָדֵי – כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts the case of «a certain animal that had two ceca. They brought it to Ravina, and he deemed it a tereifa based on» the statement «of Rav Huna» that an extra limb is like a missing limb. Since an animal missing a cecum is a tereifa, an animal with an extra cecum is likewise a tereifa. The Gemara adds: «But if they empty into each other,» such that food can move freely between them, the animal is «kosher,» because they are considered one organ.

segments.he: הָהִיא גּוּבְתָּא דַּהֲוָה נָפְקָא מִבֵּי כָסֵי לְהוּבְלִילָא, סָבַר רַב אָשֵׁי לְמִיטְרְפַהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא מָר בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: כֹּל הָנֵי חֵיוֵי בָּרָיָיתָא הָכִי אִית לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts the case of «a certain tube that exited from the reticulum into the omasum. Rav Ashi thought to deem» the animal «a tereifa. Rav Huna Mar bar Ḥiyya said to Rav Ashi: All animals» that dwell «outside have» tubes like «this,» and one need not be concerned.

segments.he: הָהוּא גּוּבְתָּא דַּהֲוָה מְעַבְּרָא מִבֵּי כָסֵי לִכְרֵסָא, סְבַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַכְשׁוֹרַהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ בַּחֲדָא מְחִיתָא מַחֵתִינְהוּ? הֵיכָא דְּאִתְּמַר – אִתְּמַר, הֵיכָא דְּלָא אִתְּמַר – לָא אִתְּמַר.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts the case of «a certain tube that passed from the reticulum to the rumen. Mar bar Rav Ashi thought to deem» the animal «kosher,» as in the above case. «Rav Oshaya said to him: Is that to say all» such cases «are woven in one weave? Where it was stated» that such an organ is normal, «it was stated; where it was not stated, it was not stated.» This animal is a tereifa.

segments.he: הֵעִיד נָתָן בַּר שֵׁילָא רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דְּצִיפּוֹרִי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי, עַל שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי מֵעַיִם הַיּוֹצְאִין מִן הַבְּהֵמָה כְּאֶחָד, שֶׁהִיא טְרֵפָה, וּכְנֶגְדָּן בָּעוֹף – כְּשֵׁרָה. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁיּוֹצְאִין בִּשְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת, אֲבָל יוֹצְאִין בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְכָלִין עַד כְּאֶצְבַּע – כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: «Natan bar Sheila, head of the butchers of Tzippori, testified before Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «about two intestines that exit» the abomasum of «the animal as one, that this» renders the animal «a tereifa. But» if this phenomenon occurs «likewise in a bird,» it is «kosher,» because it is common in birds. «In what» case «is this statement said,» i.e., that two intestines render an animal a tereifa? It is said in a case «where they exit at two different points. But» if «they exit at one point,» adjacent to each other, «and they end,» i.e., they merge into one intestine, «within a fingerbreadth,» the animal is «kosher.»

segments.he: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי, חַד אָמַר: הוּא דְּהָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי, וְחַד אָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי.
segments.en: «Rav Ami and Rav Asi disagree with regard to» this halakha. «One says: It» is kosher when the two intestines exit at one point only in a case «where they subsequently merge» into one intestine; «and one says:» It is kosher «even if they do not subsequently merge.»

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הוּא דְּהָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי, הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי ״עַד כְּאֶצְבַּע״, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָדְרִי וְעָרְבִי, מַאי ״עַד כְּאֶצְבַּע״? עַד כְּאֶצְבַּע מִלְּמַטָּה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Granted, according to the one who says» that «it» is kosher only in a case «where they subsequently merge, this» explanation is consistent with «that which» the baraita «teaches: Within a fingerbreadth.» That is, the two intestines must merge within a fingerbreadth for the animal to be kosher. «But according to the one who says:» It is kosher «even if they do not subsequently merge, what» is the meaning of the phrase: And they end «within a fingerbreadth?» The Gemara responds: It means «within a fingerbreadth below.» As long as the intestines merge before the final fingerbreadth near the anus, the animal is kosher.

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוחנן אמר: יש לו
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan: it does, and it looks like a rose petal between the wings
moves.about: reading Ḥizkiyya as meaning only that a perforated bird lung does not render it a tereifa

moves.cueHe: מאי ״אין ריאה לעוף״?
moves.summary: what does Ḥizkiyya mean by saying a bird has no lung
moves.about: what Ḥizkiyya's phrase a bird has no lungs means

moves.cueHe: אילימא דלית ליה כלל
moves.summary: floats: he means it literally has no lung at all
moves.about: Levi's baraita equating the tereifot of an animal with those of a bird

moves.cueHe: והא קא חזינן דאית ליה
moves.summary: rejects that float: we plainly see that a bird has a lung
moves.about: the floated reading that Ḥizkiyya means a bird literally has no lung — we plainly see that it does

moves.cueHe: אלא דלא מיטריף ביה
moves.summary: floats: he means a perforated lung does not make a bird a tereifa
moves.about: Levi's teaching that a bird's tereifot match an animal's

moves.cueHe: והתני לוי
moves.summary: rejects it from Levi's baraita: a bird's tereifot match an animal's
moves.about: Levi's baraita refutes the reading that a perforated lung does not make a bird a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אלא, אין לו לא לינפל ולא ליחמר
moves.summary: reads Ḥizkiyya as meaning the bird's lung has no law of falling and no law of singeing
moves.about: reading Ḥizkiyya as meaning a bird's lung has no law of falling and no law of singeing

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא?
moves.summary: why should a bird's lung be exempt from those two concerns
moves.about: why a bird's lung is exempt from the laws of falling and singeing

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חנה: הואיל ורוב צלעותיה מגינות עליה
moves.summary: Rav Ḥana: most of the bird's ribs shield the lung
moves.about: the bird's ribs protect its lung, so no damage need be suspected

moves.cueHe: והא מדאמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan's reply shows Ḥizkiyya did mean the bird has no lung at all, defeating the reinterpretation the sugya had settled on
moves.about: its own reinterpretation of Ḥizkiyya as speaking only of falling and singeing cannot stand against R' Yoḥanan's reply

moves.cueHe: אלא אמרי במערבא משמיה דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
moves.summary: the Westerners in R' Yosei b'R' Ḥanina's name: Ḥizkiyya's words simply show he was not familiar with chickens
moves.about: the Westerners transmit R' Yosei b'R' Ḥanina's verdict on Ḥizkiyya's statement

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רב: שמוטת ירך בעוף כשרה
moves.summary: Rav Huna reports Rav that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher — the opposite of Rav Yehuda's report
moves.about: Rav's ruling that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבה בר רב הונא לרב הונא: והא רבנן דאתו מפומבדיתא
moves.summary: the Pumbedita rabbis report Rav, through Rav Yehuda, as ruling it a tereifa
moves.about: whether Rav held a dislocated femur in a bird kosher, as Rav Huna reports, or a tereifa, as the Pumbedita rabbis report in Rav Yehuda's name

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: ברי, נהרא נהרא ופשטיה
moves.summary: each river and its course: Rav ruled stringently for Pumbedita's custom though he held it kosher
moves.about: different localities keep different customs, so Rav ruled stringently for Pumbedita though he himself held it kosher

moves.cueHe: אזל רבי אבא, אשכחיה לרב ירמיה בר אבא
moves.summary: R' Abba finds Rav Yirmeya bar Abba inspecting birds at the convergence of sinews
moves.about: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba's practice of inspecting birds at the convergence of sinews

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: למה ליה למר כולי האי?
moves.summary: why inspect at all, given Rav Huna's report of Rav that even a dislocated femur leaves the bird kosher
moves.about: why inspect the convergence of sinews when Rav holds that even a wholly dislocated femur leaves the bird kosher

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אנא מתניתין ידענא
moves.summary: he relies on the mishna about severed legs, which Rav himself extended to birds
moves.about: he inspects because the mishna, extended by Rav to birds, makes a removed convergence of sinews a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, קשיא דרב אדרב!
moves.summary: then Rav contradicts Rav — the extension to birds against the leniency for a dislocated femur
moves.about: Rav's extension of the mishna to birds contradicts his ruling that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: אישתיק
moves.summary: he falls silent, offering no answer
moves.about: he gave no answer at all to the contradiction R' Abba raised in Rav

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: דלמא שני ליה בין שמוטה לחתוכה?
moves.summary: R' Abba himself floats a resolution: Rav may distinguish dislocated from severed
moves.about: perhaps Rav distinguishes a dislocated femur, which leaves the bird kosher, from a severed one, which does not

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: ואת מפרשת שמעתתיה דרב?
moves.summary: do you interpret Rav by your own reasoning — Rav said the distinction explicitly
moves.about: whether one may interpret Rav's rulings by one's own reasoning when Rav stated the distinction in so many words

moves.cueHe: בפירוש אמר רב: שמוטה – כשרה, חתוכה – פסולה
moves.summary: Rav stated in so many words that dislocated is kosher and severed unfit, and one need not be surprised
moves.about: Rav stated explicitly that a dislocated femur is kosher and a severed one unfit

moves.cueHe: כי סליק רבי אבא, אשכחיה לרבי זירא
moves.summary: on going up to Eretz Yisrael R' Abba finds R' Zeira teaching the opposite report of Rav Huna
moves.about: Rav Huna's report of Rav that a dislocated femur in a bird is a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רב: שמוטת ירך בעוף טרפה
moves.summary: R' Zeira teaches Rav Huna in Rav's name as ruling it a tereifa
moves.about: Rav's ruling as R' Zeira has it — a dislocated femur in a bird is a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: חיי דמר, מיומא דסליק מר להכא
moves.summary: R' Abba swears that since R' Zeira left Babylonia they heard Rav Huna himself rule the opposite
moves.about: whether Rav Huna reported Rav as ruling a dislocated femur in a bird kosher or a tereifa

moves.cueHe: הוה לן פתחון פה קמיה דרב הונא ושאילניה, ואמר לן
moves.summary: they asked Rav Huna face to face and he said a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher
moves.about: Rav Huna told them face to face that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: ואשכחתיה נמי לרבי ירמיה בר אבא
moves.summary: R' Abba retells to R' Zeira how he found Rav Yirmeya bar Abba inspecting
moves.about: Rav Huna's report of Rav that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: ואקשי ליה: לא סבר לה מר הא דאמר רב הונא אמר רב
moves.summary: does Master not accept Rav Huna's report of Rav that a dislocated femur leaves a bird kosher
moves.about: why he inspects the convergence of sinews if he accepts Rav Huna's report of Rav that a dislocated femur leaves a bird kosher

moves.cueHe: אמר לי: אנא מתניתין ידענא
moves.summary: he answers again from the mishna as extended by Rav to birds
moves.about: he relies on the mishna together with Rav's extension of it to birds

moves.cueHe: ואמרי ליה: אי הכי, קשיא דרב אדרב!
moves.summary: then Rav contradicts Rav
moves.about: Rav's extension of the mishna to birds contradicts his ruling that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: אישתיק
moves.summary: he falls silent
moves.about: he gave no answer to the contradiction R' Abba raised in Rav

moves.cueHe: ואקשי ליה: ודלמא שני ליה לרב בין שמוטה לחתוכה?
moves.summary: perhaps Rav distinguishes dislocated from severed
moves.about: perhaps Rav distinguishes a dislocated femur from a severed one

moves.cueHe: ואמר לי: ואת מפרשת שמעתיה דרב?
moves.summary: Rav said it explicitly; do not construe his words yourself
moves.about: whether one may interpret Rav's ruling by one's own reasoning when Rav stated the distinction explicitly

moves.cueHe: ואת, מה בידך?
moves.summary: R' Abba turns back to R' Zeira: and what tradition do you hold?
moves.about: what tradition R' Zeira himself holds on a dislocated femur in a bird

moves.cueHe: הכי אמר רב חייא בר אשי אמר רב
moves.summary: R' Zeira supplies his own chain: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi in Rav's name, a tereifa
moves.about: the version of Rav's ruling that R' Zeira received — a dislocated femur in a bird is a tereifa

moves.cueHe: וכן אמר רבי יעקב בר אידי אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: and R' Ya'akov bar Idi in R' Yoḥanan's name rules likewise
moves.about: Rav's ruling that a dislocated femur in a bird is a tereifa

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יעקב בר אידי: אילמלי הוה רבי יוחנן באתרא דאורו בה חברוותא להתירא
moves.summary: had R' Yoḥanan been where the earlier assembly permitted it, he would not have stirred
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan would not have contested the earlier assembly had he been where they ruled such a bird permitted

moves.cueHe: דאמר רבי חנינא אמר רבי: שמוטת ירך בעוף כשרה
moves.summary: for R' Ḥanina reports Rabbi as permitting such a bird
moves.about: R' Ḥanina's report in Rabbi's name that a dislocated femur in a bird is kosher

moves.cueHe: ותרנגולת היתה לו לרבי חנינא שנשמטה ירך שלה
moves.summary: R' Ḥanina's own hen, permitted by Rabbi, salted and shown to students
moves.about: R' Ḥanina salted the hen and used it to teach the students that Rabbi had permitted it to him

moves.cueHe: ולית הלכתא ככל הני שמעתתא, אלא כי הא
moves.summary: the halakha follows none of these statements but the exchange of R' Yosei ben Nehorai with R' Yehoshua ben Levi
moves.about: the halakha follows none of the foregoing statements about a dislocated femur but the exchange of R' Yehoshua ben Levi, that a survival anecdote does not override the received measure

moves.cueHe: דשאל רבי יוסי בן נהוראי את רבי יהושע בן לוי: קדירת קנה בכמה?
moves.summary: how large a puncture of the windpipe makes an animal a tereifa
moves.about: how large a puncture of the windpipe renders an animal a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: משנה שלמה שנינו, עד כאיסר האיטלקי
moves.summary: an explicit mishna gives the measure of the Italian issar
moves.about: the measure is that of the Italian issar, as an explicit mishna teaches

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: והלא רחל אחת היתה בשכונתנו
moves.summary: a ewe in their neighbourhood was punctured beyond that and lived once patched with reed shell
moves.about: a ewe whose windpipe was punctured beyond the measure yet survived once patched with reed shell

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: ועל דא את סמיך?
moves.summary: do you rely on that? R' Shimon ben Ḥalafta's splinted hen lived too, and the halakha is still that it is a tereifa
moves.about: whether a single survival anecdote may be relied on against a widespread halakha

moves.cueHe: אלא מאי אית לך למימר: תוך שנים עשר חדש הוה
moves.summary: such survival is only within twelve months, and so with the ewe
moves.about: such an animal survives only within twelve months and then dies, so the ewe anecdote proves nothing

moves.cueHe: אמרו עליו על רבי שמעון בן חלפתא שעסקן בדברים היה
moves.summary: R' Shimon ben Ḥalafta was a researcher who regrew a plucked hen's down in an oven to counter R' Yehuda
moves.about: R' Shimon ben Ḥalafta was a researcher of matters who would stage experiments

moves.cueHe: ודלמא קסבר רבי יהודה טרפה משבחת?
moves.summary: perhaps R' Yehuda holds a tereifa's health can improve, so the experiment refutes nothing
moves.about: whether the regrown down actually disproves R' Yehuda's ruling

moves.cueHe: אם כן, במידי דמיטרפא בה
moves.summary: even so, not in the very organ by which it was made a tereifa
moves.about: perhaps R' Yehuda holds that a tereifa can even improve, so the regrown feathers refute nothing

moves.cueHe: מאי עסקן בדברים?
moves.summary: from what episode did the epithet researcher of matters come
moves.about: from what episode R' Shimon ben Ḥalafta earned the epithet researcher of matters

moves.cueHe: אמר רב משרשיא, דכתיב: ״לך אל נמלה עצל״
moves.summary: Rav Mesharshiyya: he set out to test Solomon's claim that the ant has no ruler
moves.about: the verse describing the ant as having no chief, overseer or ruler

moves.cueHe: אזל בתקופת תמוז, פרסיה לגלימיה אקינא דשומשמני
moves.summary: the cloak-and-shade experiment at the ant hole, ending with the ants killing the marked ant
moves.about: the shade experiment on an ant hole to test whether ants have a king

moves.cueHe: אמר: שמע מינה לית להו מלכא
moves.summary: they killed without a royal edict, so they have no king
moves.about: the ants killed their fellow without a royal edict, confirming Solomon's words that they have no king

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: ודלמא מלכא הוה בהדייהו?
moves.summary: the king may have been present, or they held his edict, or it was an interregnum
moves.about: the experiment does not prove ants have no king — the king may have been present, or licensed them, or there was an interregnum

moves.cueHe: אלא, סמוך אהימנותא דשלמה
moves.summary: the point rests on Solomon's credibility, not on the experiment
moves.about: the point rests not on the experiment but on relying on Solomon's credibility that ants have no king

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא: סימן לטרפה – שנים עשר חדש
moves.summary: Rav Huna fixes twelve months as the sign of a tereifa, taking up the twelve-month figure just used
moves.about: the baraita on the signs of a tereifa

moves.cueHe: מיתיבי: סימן לטרפה – כל שאינה יולדת
moves.summary: a baraita gives other signs — barrenness, deterioration, thirty days — but never twelve months
moves.about: no tanna in the baraita gives twelve months as the sign of a tereifa, as Rav Huna said

moves.cueHe: רבי אומר: סימן לטרפה – שלשים יום
moves.summary: inside the baraita, Rabbi sets the sign at thirty days
moves.about: what sign shows that an animal is a tereifa — inability to give birth, or failure to survive thirty days

moves.cueHe: אמרו לו: והלא הרבה מתקיימות שתים שלש שנים!
moves.summary: the Sages answer Rabbi that many certain tereifot survive two or three years
moves.about: whether thirty days can be the sign, since many certain tereifot survive two or three years

moves.cueHe: תנאי היא, דתניא
moves.summary: the signs are a tannaitic dispute, and a second baraita supplies a tanna who holds like Rav Huna
moves.about: the matter is a tannaitic dispute and Rav Huna's twelve months follows one of the tannaim

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוסי בן המשולם: מעשה בענבול
moves.summary: a man at Inbul lived with a gourd-shell patch over a missing piece of skull, so it is no tereifa
moves.about: whether a missing piece of skull renders one a tereifa, given the man at Inbul who lived with a gourd-shell patch

moves.cueHe: אמר לו רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: משם ראיה?
moves.summary: it was summer; when winter came he died at once — so a full year is the measure, as Rav Huna held
moves.about: whether the Inbul incident proves anything — it was summer, and once winter came the man died at once

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אחא בר יעקב, הלכה: טרפה יולדת ומשבחת
moves.summary: the halakha is that a tereifa can give birth and can improve, so neither proves it kosher
moves.about: whether giving birth or improving in health proves that an animal is not a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אמר אמימר: הני ביעי דטרפה
moves.summary: Ameimar opens the question of the eggs of a tereifa hen

moves.cueHe: שיחלא קמא אסירא
moves.summary: the first clutch is forbidden; later eggs have two causes and are permitted

moves.cueHe: איתיביה רב אשי לאמימר: ושוין בביצת טריפה שאסורה
moves.summary: a mishna forbids a tereifa's egg because it grew in prohibition, apparently even later eggs
moves.about: the mishna forbids the egg of a tereifa because it grew in prohibition, against Ameimar's permitting later eggs

moves.cueHe: התם בדספנא מארעא
moves.summary: that mishna speaks of an unfertilised hen, where the tereifa is the only cause
moves.about: the mishna speaks of an unfertilised egg, where the tereifa is the sole cause

moves.cueHe: ולישני ליה בשיחלא קמא?
moves.summary: why not answer instead that the mishna means the first clutch
moves.about: why Ameimar did not instead answer that the mishna refers to the first clutch of eggs

moves.cueHe: אם כן, ״גדלה״? ״גמרה״ מיבעי ליה
moves.summary: the word grew rules that out; it would have had to say was finished
moves.about: the mishna's word grew rules out the first-clutch answer; it would have had to say was finished

moves.cueHe: אלא, הא דתנן: ולד טרפה
moves.summary: on that assumption the taught dispute of R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua over the offspring of a tereifa is hard to place
moves.about: if a fetus becomes a tereifa with its mother, the Eliezer–Yehoshua dispute over the offspring of a tereifa is hard to place

moves.cueHe: במאי קא מיפלגי?
moves.summary: what case divides them
moves.about: what case underlies the dispute between R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua over the offspring of a tereifa

moves.cueHe: בשנטרפה ולבסוף עיברה
moves.summary: she was made a tereifa and then conceived; they dispute whether this-and-that-cause is permitted
moves.about: they dispute a mother rendered a tereifa and only then impregnated, i.e. whether this-and-that-cause is permitted

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, אדמיפלגי לגבוה, ליפלגו להדיוט?
moves.summary: then they should have disputed eating rather than sacrifice
moves.about: if that is the issue, they should have disputed the more basic case of eating rather than of sacrifice

moves.cueHe: להודיעך כחו דרבי יהושע
moves.summary: to convey how far R' Yehoshua's leniency reaches — even to the altar
moves.about: the case of the altar is chosen to convey how far R' Yehoshua's leniency reaches

moves.cueHe: וליפלגו להדיוט, להודיעך כחו דרבי אליעזר
moves.summary: then let them dispute eating, to convey how far R' Eliezer's stringency reaches
moves.about: they could equally have disputed the ordinary case to convey how far R' Eliezer's stringency reaches

moves.cueHe: כח דהיתרא עדיף ליה
moves.summary: the power of leniency is preferable to display
moves.about: the tanna prefers to display the reach of leniency rather than of stringency

moves.cueHe: ומודים בביצת טרפה שאסורה, בדספנא מארעא
moves.summary: on this line the mishna's concession is about an unfertilised egg, a single cause
moves.about: the mishna's concession about a tereifa's egg is limited to a hen heated by the earth, a single cause

moves.cueHe: רב אחא סבר לה כרב אחא בר יעקב
moves.summary: Rav Aḥa holds a tereifa can lay, and so teaches Ameimar in the version just discussed
moves.about: that a tereifa can give birth, and so a tereifa hen can lay eggs

moves.cueHe: רבינא לא סבר לה כדרב אחא בר יעקב
moves.summary: Ravina denies that a tereifa can lay, and so teaches Ameimar in another formulation
moves.about: whether a tereifa can become pregnant or lay eggs — Ravina does not share Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov's view that it can

moves.cueHe: אמר אמימר: הני ביעי דספק טרפה, דשיחלא קמא משהינן להו
moves.summary: Ravina's Ameimar: hold back the first clutch of a doubtful tereifa; if she lays again they are permitted
moves.about: Ravina's formulation of Ameimar's ruling, about the eggs of a bird only doubtfully a tereifa

moves.cueHe: איתיביה רב אשי לאמימר: ומודים בביצת טרפה שאסורה
moves.summary: the mishna's rule shows a tereifa bird does produce eggs
moves.about: the mishna's forbidding a tereifa's egg shows a tereifa bird can produce eggs, against Ravina's version of Ameimar

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: התם בדשיחלא קמא
moves.summary: the mishna means the first clutch, already present before she became a tereifa
moves.about: narrowing the mishna to the first clutch, which existed before the bird became a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אם כן, ״גדלה״? ״גמרה״ מבעי ליה
moves.summary: then the mishna should have said was finished, not grew
moves.about: the mishna's word grew is wrong for the first clutch; it should have said was finished

moves.cueHe: תני: גמרה
moves.summary: emend the mishna to read was finished
moves.about: emending the mishna to read was finished in place of grew

moves.cueHe: אלא, הא דתנן: ולד טרפה
moves.summary: if a tereifa cannot conceive, the Eliezer–Yehoshua dispute is again hard to place
moves.about: if a tereifa cannot become pregnant, the Eliezer–Yehoshua dispute over the offspring of a tereifa is hard to place

moves.cueHe: במאי קא מיפלגי?
moves.summary: what case divides them on this assumption
moves.about: what case underlies the dispute if a tereifa cannot conceive

moves.cueHe: כשעיברה ולבסוף נטרפה
moves.summary: she conceived and only then became a tereifa; they dispute whether a fetus is its mother's thigh
moves.about: that a fetus is considered the thigh of its mother

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, אדמיפלגי לגבוה, ליפלגו להדיוט
moves.summary: then they should have disputed eating rather than sacrifice
moves.about: if that is the issue they should have disputed the case of eating rather than of sacrifice

moves.cueHe: להודיעך כחו דרבי יהושע
moves.summary: to convey how far R' Yehoshua's leniency reaches
moves.about: the altar case conveys how far R' Yehoshua's leniency reaches

moves.cueHe: וליפלגו בהדיוט להודיעך כחו דרבי אליעזר
moves.summary: let them dispute eating, to convey R' Eliezer's stringency
moves.about: they could have disputed the ordinary case to convey how far R' Eliezer's stringency reaches

moves.cueHe: כח דהיתירא עדיף ליה
moves.summary: the power of leniency is preferable
moves.about: the tanna prefers to display the reach of leniency
